changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `apps/console/vite.config.ts` → `apps/console/vite.config.ts` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

### `.changeset/7546-chart-series-keys-declared.md`

- names `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` → `packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Every one of the six is read by `normalizeSeries` (`@object-ui/plugin-charts`, `normalizeChartSchema.ts:242-255`) and does real work in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` — `label` names the legend entry, `variant === 'comparison'` selects the muted overlay, `opacity` / `dashArray` set stroke and fill, `stack` becomes Recharts' `stackId`, `yAxis` binds the secondary axis. Any consumer of the parse output — `objectui check` / `objectui validate` via `safeValidateSchema`, a JSON schema derived from the mirror, or any pipeline that keeps `parse()`'s result — lost them outright.

### `.changeset/8632-malformed-picklist-option-loud.md`

- names `packages/i18n/README.md` → `packages/i18n/README.md` — edited by this change

  > Two new strings land in the designer's own `en` / `zh` tables — the metadata-admin console owns its strings in `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` and is deliberately outside the ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/README.md`, "Scope — the `engine.*` carve-out").

### `.changeset/9615-locale-count-ten.md`

- names `packages/i18n/README.md` → `packages/i18n/README.md` — edited by this change

  > Correcting the numeral to ten was weighed and refused. A restated count is the construct that permitted the error, and this repository has now watched it recur three times over the same fact — objectui#3351 in a changeset file, objectui#7989 in `packages/i18n/README.md`, and this one in published source. So the number is **gone** rather than corrected: the sentence now claims only what it needs (the key is translated in every locale the package ships) and names `all-locales-key-parity.test.ts` as the instrument that re-derives it. That test asserts the stronger invariant — every pack defines every `en` key — over whatever the pack set is on the day it runs, so an eleventh pack makes the sentence more true rather than false, and there is no figure left to rot (AGENTS.md commandment #9).

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `9f0c84a44` (merge-base with origin/main): 15 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1667 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2261 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36386759548)

The **eager closure** is every chunk the entry reaches through static imports — what the browser fetches and parses before the app renders. The entry chunk on its own is a small fraction of it.

| Per-chunk ceilings | ✅ pass |

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8559187c4a1e12eabf5afa3d28ca90aec94d4fa3`

Read: card objectui#10866 (body, triage `5861646819`, seat 2's release note `5863305580`, claim `5863746430`, dev report `5864266391`), PR objectui#10886 and its record `5862881358`, PR objectui#10901 (body, diff, 14 files, 43 check-runs on the head), the objectui tree at head and at `origin/main` `9f0c84a44`, objectstack ADR-0053 and `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`. Re-measured in a private worktree at head, on the forks pool with `OBJECTUI_DATE_ZONE_CHILD=1`: the four pins over head, over the base blobs of the five sources, and over an ablation of the two ISO arms; plus a throwaway probe of core `FormulaFunctions`, `generateTimeScaleHeaders` and the i18n helpers under `America/Los_Angeles`, `Asia/Shanghai` and `UTC`. The dev report was read as a claim and checked, not adopted.

### ① Derived judgments

**Blocking**

1. **CI is red on the head, and this diff causes it.** `Bundle Analysis` (run `36383523471`, step `Check console performance budget`, comment `5864278471`) fails on the eager-closure gate's membership half: "Per-chunk membership (declared packages)" objects while every byte ceiling passes. The merge base `origin/main` `9f0c84a44` passed the same workflow three minutes earlier and PR objectui#10902 passed it five minutes later, so the diff is the variable. Mechanism, read from `apps/console/vite.config.ts` and `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` (⛔ not rebuilt here; the job log sits behind a host this session cannot reach): the `i18n-runtime` group (priority 83) carries no `includeDependenciesRecursively: false`, so it captures its members' imports recursively at rolldown's default, and it outranks `framework` (priority 80), whose declared packages `core`, `react` and `types` must land in `framework` wholly (`PER_CHUNK_MEMBERSHIP`, an exact claim). On base no `packages/i18n` module retains a runtime import of `@object-ui/core` (`utils/number-display.ts` is a re-export nothing consumes at runtime; `builtinAggregateLabels.ts` imports a type). This PR adds the first: `utils/formatting.ts` and `utils/spec-formatters.ts` import `toDisplayDate` and `isRealCalendarDate`, and `formatting.ts` is retained through app-shell's `relativeTime.ts`. So `packages/core/src/index.ts` and `utils/date-display.ts` are written into `i18n-runtime`, and `core` no longer lands wholly in `framework`. That is the objectui#9345 shape the config's own `data-adapter` paragraph records, with its repair: declare `includeDependenciesRecursively: false` on `i18n-runtime`, re-check the circular-chunk caveat that paragraph says a group taking the flag re-checks rather than inherits, and show `Bundle Analysis` green on the new head. `check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` pins the flag on `data-adapter` and the carve-out groups and asserts only that `framework` has no options tail, so nothing there moves. `apps/console/vite.config.ts` is outside claim `5863746430`'s surface: the seat amends the claim. ⛔ Copying `toDisplayDate` into `@object-ui/i18n` is not a repair (one home, objectui#4576 and objectui#10110).

**Per site, re-measured on head: 50 of 50 cases pass in both zones, every rig case among them.**

- Site 3 (`ObjectTimeline` bucket and sort, `renderer.tsx` `formatDate`). Los Angeles at clock `2026-10-06T12:00Z`: the feed of `2026-10-06` and `2026-10-07` reads `Today: Ship (10/6/2026)`, `Tomorrow: Review (10/7/2026)` (base: `Overdue: Ship (10/5/2026)`, `Today: Review (10/6/2026)`); the mixed feed reads `Overdue: Instant (10/5/2026)`, `Today: Day (10/6/2026)`; `2026-10-06` prints `10/6/2026`, `October 6, 2026` and `2026-10-06`. Shanghai: the same days; the instant `2026-10-06T04:00Z` keeps its local day in each zone and its ISO face keeps `2026-10-06` in both. Bucket, sort and face read alike.
- Site 4 (`AdvancedChartImpl` `formatTick`). Los Angeles: `2026-09-01`, `2026-09-02` tick `Sep 1`, `Sep 2` (base `Aug 31`, `Sep 1`); the month axis `Sep 2026`, `Dec 2026` (base `Aug 2026`, `Nov 2026`); a refused locale falls back to the stored days in both zones; the instants `2026-09-02T03:00Z`, `2026-09-03T03:00Z` tick `Sep 1`, `Sep 2` in Los Angeles and `Sep 2`, `Sep 3` in Shanghai, and their fallback keeps the UTC day in both.
- Site 6 (i18n). Los Angeles at 10:00 on August 30th: `formatDate('2026-09-01')` `Sep 1, 2026` (base `Aug 31, 2026`); `formatDateTime` `Sep 1, 2026, 12:00 AM` (base `Aug 31, 2026, 5:00 PM`); `formatRelativeTime` `in 2 days` (base `tomorrow`); `formatDateSpec` with `timeZone: 'America/New_York'` `Sep 1, 2026` (base `Aug 31, 2026` in BOTH zones). Shanghai: the same faces; the instant `2026-09-02T03:00Z` reads `Sep 1` in Los Angeles and `Sep 2` in Shanghai and keeps its `timeZone` day.
- Base blobs of the five sources under the head pins: 16 of 50 cases red, every Los Angeles row of the four sites among them, plus the two Shanghai rows that move on the time or on `timeZone`, and the suite-zone rows for the refused day and the throws. The reds are the reasons the pins name (`expected 'Aug 31, 2026' to be 'Sep 1, 2026'`, `RangeError: Invalid time value`, `RangeError: Value need to be finite number`).
- Ablation of the two ISO arms (the renderer's `if (isRealCalendarDate(dateString)) return toDateInputValue(date);` deleted; the chart fallback reduced to `return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);`): exactly the two Shanghai rows red (`expected '2026-10-05' to be '2026-10-06'`; `expected [ '2026-08-31', '2026-09-01' ] to deeply equal [ '2026-09-01', '2026-09-02' ]`), 48 of 50 green. The east-of-UTC rows catch a parse-only repair, as the dev says.

**The behaviour beyond a parse swap.** All three are right, pinned and named in the changeset: the `iso` face printing a refused or unparsable value as written (base threw `RangeError: Invalid time value` during render; pinned in `TimelineRenderer.dateOnlyZone-10866`); the sort sinking a refused value with the dateless items (its bucket is already "No date", and the vertical renderer groups ADJACENT items, so any other order splits a bucket; pinned through the mixed feed); `formatRelativeTime` returning an unparsable value as its string (base threw from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat.prototype.format`; pinned). Each is needed because the shared step refuses `2026-02-30`, which the engine rolled into March.

**`formatDateSpec` applies `timeZone` to an instant only: right, and the only arm the binding text allows.** The shared step's local midnight reads back as its day only in the local zone, so handing `Intl` another `timeZone` would name the day before in every zone west of the viewer's. No author who relied on the old behaviour loses the day: `timeZone: 'UTC'` or an east zone named the stored day before and still does (`Sep 1, 2026` with `timeZone: 'UTC'` in all three zones, measured); a west zone named the day before, which is the defect. What moves is the time face of a date-only value under `timeStyle`: `dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'long', timeZone: 'Asia/Tokyo'` now prints `Sep 1, 2026, 12:00:00 AM PDT` in Los Angeles (measured), where base printed the UTC midnight as 9:00 AM Tokyo. The changeset names the rule ("applies its `timeZone` to an instant only, and formats a date-only value in the local zone") and the PR body names the `timeStyle` face; that is enough for a `patch`.

**The chart span keeps the engine parse: sound.** It is a duration between two categories of one axis. Two date-only values are UTC midnights a whole number of days apart in every zone; two local midnights differ by an hour across a DST change, so a span near the 62-day bound would flip faces. An instant pair is the same under either parse.

**Site-3 census: four reads, as the dev says.** Bucket, sort, `formatDate`, and the gantt-variant axis, which is left. Measured on head: `generateTimeScaleHeaders('day', '2026-10-05', '2026-10-07', 'en-US')` reads `Oct 4, Oct 5, Oct 6` in Los Angeles and `Oct 5, Oct 6, Oct 7` in Shanghai; the `month` scale over the fourth quarter reads `Sep 2026, Oct 2026, Nov 2026` in Los Angeles. Nothing else in the two packages parses a date-only value with `new Date` or date-fns: the remaining engine parses are the gantt variant (`generateTimeScaleHeaders`, `calculateDateRange`, `calculateBarDimensions`, `findUnusableGanttDate`, the min-over-max guard, and `emptyGanttDateRange`'s `today`, a UTC day the dev's list does not name), the "now" clocks, and the chart span. ③ names the disagreement this leaves inside the gantt variant.

**Pins.** Four `PINS` rows registered the slice-1 way plus one header sentence; each zone opens with a rig case and, west, a fixture-validity case; each pin carries an instant control; the suite-zone cases run in the normal run.
